acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Minotaurs family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Charger, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Horn-Lane Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Thick neck, iron-capped horns, brass nose ring, chest scars, and a single-bladed axe replace the Bull-kin's rangy outline.
Signature mechanic: Capped Run: iron horn caps define a straight charge; on impact or miss, the Charger pivots only toward its axe side.
battlefieldDuty: Repeat front-line pressure through a fixed horn charge followed by a single-bladed axe sweep on the outside flank.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe construction: T1 Bull-kin keeps short uncapped horns, a rope harness, wooden maul, and unarmored hide while knotted rope vanes and hollow wooden whistle holes mark pressure; T2–T5 may add hollow horn flutes, slotted bronze caps, sail-cut hide, chain vanes, and vented weapon faces supported by their equipment.

Motion gains directional pressure grammar: the T1 rope and tail align with its planted stance while a still pocket forms behind the short inside horn, and later tiers lift chain slack or weapon vanes before release.
counterplay: Leave the fixed lane toward the non-axe side, then attack the exposed neck before the one-way pivot finishes. Affinity signal: T1 Bull-kin points its rope vanes and tail down one lane while the planted hoof and short inside horn remain still; T2–T5 sound hollow horns and align harness or chain vanes, exposing the silent inside cap or flute.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only pale hide without flutes, vanes, and directional pressure
Glow-only wind treatment without a force route and still center
Weightless floating that erases the family's committed mass
Dust clouds that conceal hooves, horn lane, or chain slack
identityInvariants: A bull head, bovine snout and ears, wide horns, vastly overbuilt humanoid torso, digitigrade hooved legs, and thick tail remain legible at every tier.
Deep russet and black hide, bronze, ox-blood red, and bone define the family palette.
Coarse hair, horn, bronze, heavy leather harness, chain, and hewn stone remain distinct load-bearing materials.
Nose rings, horn caps, brands, arena trophies, and chained slabs communicate rank through visible history and repairs.
Weapon mass and horn spread always preserve a readable commitment direction and recovery side.
telegraph: The brass nose ring stops swinging, the thick neck lowers, and both iron-capped horns align before the hooves accelerate.
